title: Energy, Work and Power Module 3 Lesson 2: Power From Work Done Over Time custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A machine performs $42000\text{ J}$ of work in a time of $35\text{ s}$. Calculate, in $\text{kW}$, the average power developed by the machine.
An electric motor operates at a constant power of $4.5\text{ kW}$ for $2\text{ minutes}$. Calculate, in $\text{kJ}$, the total work done by the motor.

A crane raises a container of mass $600\text{ kg}$ vertically upwards through a height of $14\text{ m}$ at a constant speed in a time of $28\text{ s}$. Assuming no resistance, calculate the power of the crane. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A hoist raises a crate of mass $180\text{ kg}$ vertically through $15\text{ m}$ in $20\text{ s}$ against a constant resistance force of $120\text{ N}$. Calculate the average power developed by the hoist. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A water pump raises $500\text{ kg}$ of water from a well of depth $18\text{ m}$ in $45\text{ s}$. The water is delivered at the top of the well at negligible speed. Calculate, in $\text{kW}$, the average power output of the pump. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A worker pulls a sledge along horizontal ice a distance of $48\text{ m}$ in $16\text{ s}$ against a constant frictional resistance of $75\text{ N}$ at a steady speed. Calculate the power developed by the worker.

questions.prompt: An elevator of mass $800\text{ kg}$ carrying a load of mass $400\text{ kg}$ is raised vertically upwards from rest through a height of $25\text{ m}$ in a time of $20\text{ s}$ at constant speed. A constant frictional resistance of $300\text{ N}$ opposes the motion. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total work done by the elevator's motor during the ascent.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find, in $\text{kW}$, the average power output of the motor.

questions.prompt: A lorry of mass $15000\text{ kg}$ travels along a straight level road. The engine works at a constant power. During a $12\text{ s}$ interval, the work done by the driving force of the engine is $720000\text{ J}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the power developed by the lorry's engine in $\text{kW}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: There is a constant resistance to motion of magnitude $1800\text{ N}$. Calculate the driving force and acceleration of the lorry at the instant when its speed is $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

questions.prompt: A car of mass $1000\text{ kg}$ travels along a straight horizontal road. It accelerates from a speed of $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to a speed of $22\text{ m s}^{-1}$ over a distance of $160\text{ m}$ in a time of $10\text{ s}$. A constant resistance to motion of $500\text{ N}$ acts on the car throughout.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the increase in kinetic energy of the car and the work done against the resistance force.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use the work-energy principle to find the total work done by the driving force of the engine, and calculate the average power developed by the engine in $\text{kW}$.

questions.prompt: A pump is used to draw water from a reservoir and project it out of a nozzle. The pump raises $1200\text{ kg}$ of water per minute through a vertical height of $15\text{ m}$. The water is ejected from the nozzle at a speed of $18\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: For each minute of operation, calculate the gain in gravitational potential energy of the water and the kinetic energy imparted to the water.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the total work done by the pump in one minute, and calculate the rate at which the pump is working in $\text{kW}$.

questions.prompt: A ski tow pulls $20\text{ skiers}$, each of average mass $75\text{ kg}$, up a slope of length $300\text{ m}$ inclined at $12^\circ$ to the horizontal. The tow moves at a constant speed of $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The average resistance to the motion of each skier is $40\text{ N}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total time taken for a skier to travel the length of the slope, and find the total resistance force opposing the $20\text{ skiers}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the total work done by the ski tow in moving the $20\text{ skiers}$ up the slope, and determine the power required by the motor in $\text{kW}$.

questions.prompt: Water flows from an elevated reservoir through a pipe of vertical drop $80\text{ m}$ into a turbine. The water enters the top of the pipe at $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and emerges at the turbine at $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Water passes through the turbine at a rate of $450\text{ kg s}^{-1}$. Frictional losses along the pipe dissipate $120\text{ kJ}$ per tonne of water. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: For each kilogram of water, calculate the potential energy lost, the kinetic energy gained, and the energy dissipated by friction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total rate at which kinetic energy is delivered to the turbine in $\text{kW}$, and if the turbine converts $85\%$ of this kinetic energy into electricity, calculate the electrical power output in $\text{kW}$.

questions.prompt: A car of mass $1200\text{ kg}$ travels along a straight road divided into two sections, $AB$ and $BC$. The section $AB$ is horizontal and of length $900\text{ m}$. Along $AB$, the car travels at a constant speed of $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with the engine working at constant power $P$. A constant resistance of $840\text{ N}$ opposes the motion along $AB$. At $B$, the road becomes inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\theta = 0.05$, and the resistance increases to $960\text{ N}$. The car ascends $BC$ maintaining the same engine power $P$, reaching a new constant steady speed $V$ at $C$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the time taken to travel from $A$ to $B$, and find the power $P$ of the engine in $\text{kW}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total opposing force on the car along the inclined section $BC$, and determine the new steady speed $V$ and the total work done by the engine in a $40\text{ s}$ climb along $BC$.
